# Picker unit test leaks focus history into a later test

## Context

The [hosted Engine unit run](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/44973418604/job/137057980710) failed in `test/playwright/unit/manager/Focus.spec.mjs:255`. The dispatcher test expected only `focus-origin` in the focus history and saw `null` as well. Its isolated retry passed.

## The Problem

The Picker ownership test at `test/playwright/unit/form/field/Picker.spec.mjs:123` sends simulated focus events with its synthetic field's unset window ID. It leaves the resulting `history.null` entry in the module singleton. The Focus dispatcher test fails when it follows Picker on the same worker.

On hosted source `a7dfa6d0a6853799f69c6c14667b971117f7a376` the dispatcher test passes alone. The two-test run below deterministically produced the same extra key. The relevant files match `dev` at `c916b512ee`.

## The Architectural Reality

The Picker test owns the simulated window events. `FocusManager.removeWindow(windowId)` already removes that window's history and pending focus-out record. The dispatcher test intentionally asserts which keys the event envelope writes.

## The Fix

Give Picker’s simulated focus events a fixture-owned window ID and remove that exact window on teardown. Keep the dispatcher test's origin assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Picker ownership and Focus dispatcher tests both pass in order on one worker with retries disabled.
- [ ] The Picker fixture releases its simulated history and pending focus-out state through `removeWindow`.

```sh
npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/form/field/Picker.spec.mjs test/playwright/unit/manager/Focus.spec.mjs --grep 'the field owns its picker|the production dispatcher retains envelope origin' --workers=1 --retries=0
```

## Out of Scope

Production focus routing and component focus policy remain in their existing owners.
